flagged.claim: The evidence cited as [1] [5] does not state this claim: “The grader model was chosen because recall was the decisive metric: the 4‑billion‑parameter candidate rejected four questions that the corpus actually answered,”

evidence.1: Slack thread in #all-groundwork started by Manav Goel with 3 message(s). Manav Goel: Should the grader use a bigger model? Manav Goel: Tested both. qwen3:8b scores 0.900 sufficiency accuracy against llama3.2:3b at 0.950, and takes 15s per call against 3.4s. qwen3:4b is worse still: accuracy 0.800 and recall drops from 1.000 to 0.717. Manav Goel: Recall is what decides it. The 4b model rejects four questions the corpus genuinely answers. A grader that keeps junk gets caught by citation validation
evidence.2: els originally chosen were retired by Groq mid-plan, which is why model ids are configuration. Roles use different models: locally that was impossible because one model had to serve both on 16GB, and hosted it is required because rate limits count per model. Measured on the same 20 grading cases: gpt-oss-20b scores 0.950 with 3/3 refusals at 234ms, against llama3.2:3b at 0.950, 2 of 3, and 3270ms. The first attempt graded only 8 of 20 and silently degraded the rest, so the client now retries onc
evidence.5: Git commit 5e7d922bbbfd0d4504507fa6379c141c6749371a by Manav0411. Commit message: measure Qwen3-4B as a grader and reject it At 2.5GB it was the obvious candidate for a memory-constrained deployment box. Measured on the same 20 cases it is the worst of the three: accuracy 0.800 against 0.950, and recall 1.000 -> 0.717. Recall is what decides it.
